m.title: Abstraction and Decomposition · worked example
m.q: A school wants a library loan system. Demonstrate decomposition and abstraction for this task. [6 marks]
st: Students must search for and borrow books, while staff track returns.
Decompose into search catalogue, check availability, record loan and record return.
Abstract away cover colour or shelf decorations; retain book ID, borrower ID and due date. [6]

w: Decompose an online ticket-booking system into three tasks. [3]
Display available tickets [1], accept and validate a booking [1], record payment or issue confirmation [1].
Explain two pieces of information to retain in a parcel-tracking system and one to ignore. [3]
Retain parcel ID [1] and delivery status/location [1]; ignore driver's favourite music [1].
Explain why decomposition makes a complex program easier to develop. [4]
Smaller modules are easier to understand [1] and assign to developers [1]; individual parts can be tested [1], making errors easier to isolate [1].

Explain how decomposition and abstraction differ. [4]

Source: Original OCR J277-style practice question.
Decomposition splits a large problem into smaller parts [1] to manage complexity [1]. Abstraction hides/removes irrelevant detail [1] to focus on what matters [1].
v: Breaking a problem into smaller parts.
Removing irrelevant details while retaining essential ones.
Smaller task that contributes to the overall solution.
x: A trace table can help check how values change during a program.
r: State one difference between lossless and lossy compression.
Lossless restores original data; lossy discards some permanently.
How does Unicode differ from standard ASCII?
Unicode supports far more characters and writing systems than the limited ASCII repertoire.
State the roles of the ALU and Control Unit.
ALU carries out arithmetic/logic; CU decodes instructions and coordinates their execution.
Why is a parcel's delivery status more relevant than its colour?
Status directly supports tracking; colour usually does not.
